summary: Each source listed in bibliography_include must be cited by a citation record.
limits: It does not read manuscript files. For a project that has them, it reports that it could not check.

findings.message: A source is listed for the built bibliography but cited nowhere.
findings.why: The bibliography would list a work the book never cites, or a citation you meant to make is missing.
suggestions: Cite it, remove it from bibliography_include in stemma.json, or keep it on purpose and record why.

findings.message: Whether a listed source is cited could not be checked: there is no manuscript and there are no citation records.
findings.why: An unused bibliography entry would go unnoticed.
suggestions: Add citation records for the citations in your manuscript, or run this again once the manuscript is in the project.

findings.message: Whether a listed source is cited could not be checked: this version does not read the files in manuscript/.
findings.why: The manuscript, not the citation records, says what is cited now, so a guess could be wrong either way.
suggestions: Nothing to fix in your files. Check this entry by hand.

findings.message: Whether a listed source is cited could not be checked: at least one citation record cannot be read.
findings.why: The unreadable file may be the citation of this source.
suggestions: Repair the unreadable citation record first (see the record.valid finding), then run `check` again.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: Each citation record's key must name exactly one source record.
limits: Reads citation records only, not manuscript files. It does not show that a source supports a sentence.

findings.message: A citation uses a key that no source record holds.
findings.why: A reader or a build cannot tell which source this citation means, so it cannot be checked or put in the bibliography.
suggestions: Correct the key in the citation, or add a source record with that key (or add it to the right source's key_aliases).

findings.message: A citation uses a key that more than one source record holds.
findings.why: A reader or a build cannot tell which source this citation means, so it cannot be checked or put in the bibliography.
suggestions: Give each source its own key.

findings.message: A citation record names no citation key and no source.
findings.why: A reader or a build cannot tell which source this citation means, so it cannot be checked or put in the bibliography.
suggestions: Add the key of the source being cited, or remove the citation.

findings.message: A citation's key could not be looked up because at least one source record cannot be read.
findings.why: The unreadable file may or may not be the source this citation means.
suggestions: Repair the unreadable source record first (see the record.valid finding), then run `check` again.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: Warns about written map coordinates in project files, without repeating the value.
limits: Recognizes only geo: addresses, degrees with N, S, E and W, and comma-separated decimal pairs with at least three decimal places. It cannot tell whether a site is restricted.

findings.message: Text in a project file looks like a map coordinate. The value is not repeated here.
findings.why: This output can disclose a restricted site's position. The scan cannot tell whether a site is restricted, so it warns about every coordinate it recognizes.
suggestions: Look at the position in the evidence. If it is a sensitive site, remove the value from the file (git history may still hold it). If it is public or not a coordinate, you need do nothing.

findings.message: A project file could not be read, so it was not scanned for coordinates.
findings.why: This output can disclose a restricted site's position. The scan cannot tell whether a site is restricted, so it warns about every coordinate it recognizes.
suggestions: Make the file a readable UTF-8 file inside the project, then run `check` again.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: Each DOI or library identifier on a source record must have a saved lookup that names the same work.
limits: It compares titles. Only identifiers Stemma can look up are tested; others are reported as not checked.

findings.message: An identifier on the source record has not been looked up.
findings.why: An identifier that resolves nowhere, or to another work, sends a reader to the wrong thing.
suggestions: Nothing needs doing. `resolve` looks up DOIs at Crossref and Internet Archive items; other identifiers cannot yet be looked up.

findings.message: A catalogue did not find the work this identifier should name.
findings.why: An identifier that resolves nowhere, or to another work, sends a reader to the wrong thing.
suggestions: Check the identifier against the work and correct or remove it.

findings.message: An identifier resolves to a work with a different title.
findings.why: An identifier that resolves nowhere, or to another work, sends a reader to the wrong thing.
suggestions: Check which is wrong: the identifier or the record's title.

findings.message: The saved lookup states no title, or the record has none, so the identifier could not be compared.
findings.why: An identifier that resolves nowhere, or to another work, sends a reader to the wrong thing.
suggestions: Nothing needs doing. It is compared once both state a title.

findings.message: The saved lookup is a response that could not be read.
findings.why: An identifier that resolves nowhere, or to another work, sends a reader to the wrong thing.
suggestions: Nothing needs doing. Running `resolve` again replaces it.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: A citation's page or other locator must fall inside the extent recorded on the source or, for pages, folios, chapters and paragraphs, inside what the source files hold.
limits: It tests range only, not that anything is on that page. Source files made from part of a work cover only that part. It reads citation records only.

findings.message: A citation's locator is outside the extent recorded for the work.
findings.why: A page or other locator that is not in the work sends a reader nowhere, and is a common sign of an invented or mistyped citation.
suggestions: Check the locator against the work and correct it. If the recorded extent is wrong, correct the source record.

findings.message: A cited page, chapter or paragraph is outside those in your source files.
findings.why: A page or other locator that is not in the work sends a reader nowhere, and is a common sign of an invented or mistyped citation.
suggestions: Check the number against the source and correct it. If it is right, your source file holds only part of the work or leaves that page without a label.

findings.message: A cited page falls between labelled pages, on a page with no established label, so it could not be checked.
findings.why: Until the locator can be compared with the work's pages or extent, a wrong one would go unnoticed.
suggestions: Look at the page. If its number can be established, add it to the page map and run `source label`.

findings.message: A locator could not be checked: no extent is recorded for it, and no source file has its numbering.
findings.why: Until the locator can be compared with the work's pages or extent, a wrong one would go unnoticed.
suggestions: For pages, label your source file's pages; a source with no pages cannot check a page number. For another kind of locator, record the work's extent on the source, taken from the work itself.

findings.message: A locator is not written in a form that can be compared with the work's pages or extent.
findings.why: Until the locator can be compared with the work's pages or extent, a wrong one would go unnoticed.
suggestions: Write it as the printed label, or as a range with both ends in full, such as 41-43. Otherwise check it by hand.

findings.message: A locator could not be checked: a source file of this source cannot be read or is damaged.
findings.why: Until the locator can be compared with the work's pages or extent, a wrong one would go unnoticed.
suggestions: See the record.valid and source.pages findings, repair the source file, then run `check` again.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: A source record's title, authors, year and venue are compared with saved catalogue lookups.
limits: It reads saved responses and does not go to the network. A catalogue can be wrong, or describe another edition or a whole set.

findings.message: The source record disagrees with a saved catalogue lookup.
findings.why: A reference with the wrong author, title or year points readers to the wrong work, and is a common sign of an invented or confused citation.
suggestions: Compare both with the work itself. Correct the record if it is wrong. A catalogue can be wrong or describe another edition: if so, keep the record and the finding shows the difference.

findings.message: The source's details have not been compared with any catalogue: no lookup that found the work is saved.
findings.why: A reference with the wrong author, title or year points readers to the wrong work, and is a common sign of an invented or confused citation.
suggestions: Nothing needs doing. `resolve` compares the source once an identifier is known; some works are in no catalogue it reads.

findings.message: A saved lookup states no title, so no title could be compared with it.
findings.why: A reference with the wrong author, title or year points readers to the wrong work, and is a common sign of an invented or confused citation.
suggestions: Nothing needs doing. A lookup by another identifier may state one.

findings.message: A saved lookup is for one volume of a set and gives the set's date, and nothing else here shows the volume's year or contradicts it.
findings.why: A reference with the wrong author, title or year points readers to the wrong work, and is a common sign of an invented or confused citation.
suggestions: Nothing needs doing. A catalogue record that dates the volume, or a copy with a clearer title page text, would corroborate the year.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: A source record's title, authors, year and venue are compared with what its captured copy states about itself and with the text of its title page.
limits: It applies to sources that have source files. A value that recognized text garbles is reported as not found, which a person can confirm by looking. It shows disagreement, not which side is right.

findings.message: The source record disagrees with what the captured copy states about itself.
findings.why: A reference with the wrong author, title or year points readers to the wrong work, and is a common sign of an invented or confused citation.
suggestions: Compare both values with the title page of the work. Correct the record if it is wrong; if the copy is a different edition or a misdescribed file, capture the right one.

findings.message: The source's details could not be compared with a copy: its source file is damaged.
findings.why: A reference with the wrong author, title or year points readers to the wrong work, and is a common sign of an invented or confused citation.
suggestions: See the source.pages finding and repair the source file.

findings.message: Some of the source's details are shown neither by the copy's title page text nor by a saved catalogue record, and nothing contradicts them.
findings.why: A reference with the wrong author, title or year points readers to the wrong work, and is a common sign of an invented or confused citation.
suggestions: Nothing needs doing: this is a limit of what was covered. A saved lookup or a copy with a clearer text would corroborate more. The author may also record what the title page shows (`review add --scope source_details`).

findings.message: The source record has no title yet, so its details could not be compared with the copy.
findings.why: A reference with the wrong author, title or year points readers to the wrong work, and is a common sign of an invented or confused citation.
suggestions: Nothing needs doing. Once a title is recorded, it is compared.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: A figure in a sentence that cites one source must be in that source's text.
limits: It finds the figure anywhere in the source, not necessarily where cited or with the same meaning. Figures written as words are not read.

findings.message: A figure in a sentence that cites this source was not found in the source's text.
findings.why: A figure attributed to a source that does not hold it misreports the source.
suggestions: Find the figure in the source and correct the sentence, or move the figure to a sentence that does not attribute it to this source. A converted or recognized text can also be wrong: look at the page.

findings.message: A sentence with a figure cites more than one source, so which one holds the figure could not be judged.
findings.why: A figure attributed to a source that does not hold it misreports the source.
suggestions: Nothing needs doing. A sentence that cites one source has its figures looked for there.

findings.message: A figure could not be compared: the source has no usable text.
findings.why: A figure attributed to a source that does not hold it misreports the source.
suggestions: Capture or repair the source's text.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: The repository must hold no binary file, such as a Word, PDF or image file. It reads the files git tracks or would add.
limits: A file that git ignores is not read. A file already removed stays in git history, which this does not read.

findings.message: A binary file is in the repository, or would be added to it. A project holds text; originals and other binary files stay outside.
findings.why: git cannot show what changed in a binary, keeps every version for good, and nothing in it can be searched, checked or cited.
suggestions: Keep the file where the author holds it, outside the repository. To read or cite it, convert it with `source convert`: the Markdown in sources/ is tied to the original by its hash. For a format Stemma does not convert, note what it is, its hash and where it is held.
Moving the file out is the author's decision. A file already committed stays in git history until the history is rewritten.

summary: Where a citation gives a quotation and a locator, the quoted words must be on that page, or in that chapter or paragraph.
limits: It relies on the page labels in the source files. Where a part has no label, it reports that it could not check.

findings.message: The quoted words are in the source, but not where the citation says.
findings.why: A reader who turns to the cited place and does not find the words cannot check them.
suggestions: Look at the place found, and correct the citation's locator, ideally by citing a captured passage so that the locator is copied.

findings.message: The quotation runs beyond what the citation names, for example over a page break.
findings.why: A reader who turns to the cited place and does not find the words cannot check them.
suggestions: Cite every page the words lie on, as a captured passage does.

findings.message: Where the quoted words lie could not be compared with the locator: that part of the text has no such page label, chapter or paragraph.
findings.why: A reader who turns to the cited place and does not find the words cannot check them.
suggestions: Establish the page labels (`source pages`, `source label`) from what shows them, or cite a locator the source's text has.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: Each quotation held by a citation record must be in the text of the cited source's files, apart from six harmless differences: white space and line breaks, soft hyphens, Latin ligatures, two Unicode spellings of the same characters, straight against curly quotation marks of the same level, and a word the text splits with a hyphen at a line end. Captured passages, note extracts and the quoted words of anchored passages are compared too. A close but different passage is shown beside the quotation.
limits: A pass is agreement with the source text, which can be wrong, especially where it comes from character recognition. The cited page is tested by quote.page. Joining a line-end hyphen can pass a quotation that drops a hyphen belonging to the word; the report names each join. It does not read manuscript files.

findings.message: A quotation is not in the source's text as written. A passage close to it is; both are shown.
findings.why: Readers take quoted words to be the source's own. Words the source does not hold misreport it.
suggestions: Compare the two texts, and look at the page itself, since converted or recognized text can be wrong. If your quotation is wrong, capture the passage by its address so the words are copied. An omission, an added word, a change of capitals or punctuation, an ellipsis or a bracketed edit all count as differences.

findings.message: A quotation was not found in the source's text.
findings.why: Readers take quoted words to be the source's own. Words the source does not hold misreport it.
suggestions: Find the words (`passage find`) and capture them, or remove the quotation marks if these are your words or a paraphrase. If the page does hold these words, the source text is wrong there, or it is a different edition: record that, or capture the copy you quoted.

findings.message: A passage record no longer matches the words at its address.
findings.why: Readers take quoted words to be the source's own. Words the source does not hold misreport it.
suggestions: Do not edit the record's words. Capture the passage again from the source text and retire this one.

findings.message: A citation made from a passage no longer says what the passage says: its quotation or locator was changed.
findings.why: Readers take quoted words to be the source's own. Words the source does not hold misreport it.
suggestions: Add the citation again from the passage, so that both are copied, and retire this one.

findings.message: A quotation could not be compared: the text of its source cannot be used here.
findings.why: Until the quotation can be compared with the source's text, it is unchecked.
suggestions: See the source.held and source.pages findings, then capture or repair the source's text.

findings.message: A quotation was not found, but the only text is marked poor, so this does not show that the source lacks it.
findings.why: Until the quotation can be compared with the source's text, it is unchecked.
suggestions: Look at the page itself, or capture a better text.

findings.message: A note extract could not be compared: none of the passages it is anchored to can be found in the source text.
findings.why: Until the quotation can be compared with the source's text, it is unchecked.
suggestions: See the findings on its passages, and anchor the note to a passage that is in the text.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: Reads stemma.json, every record file and the rule headings in rules.md.
limits: For some record kinds, rules beyond the record shape are not checked. A report says so when such a record is present.

findings.message: A file cannot be read as a record, so nothing in it was checked.
findings.why: Every other check reads these files. A broken record can hide a citation problem or create a false one.
suggestions: Open the named file and repair it (look for merge-conflict markers, a repeated key or a missing bracket), or restore it from git. Stemma does not guess its content.

findings.message: A file was written in a newer record format than this version reads, so it was not checked.
findings.why: Every other check reads these files. A broken record can hide a citation problem or create a false one.
suggestions: Update Stemma before changing this file. This version will not rewrite it.

findings.message: A file is not written in the canonical form (key order, indentation or line endings differ).
findings.why: Digests, review marks and diffs depend on one exact form. No value is wrong because of this alone.
suggestions: Run `fmt` on the file. It rewrites the layout and changes no value.

findings.message: A record breaks a rule of the record format.
findings.why: Every other check reads these files. A broken record can hide a citation problem or create a false one.
suggestions: Correct the field named in the evidence, then run `check` again.

findings.message: A file under records/ or sources/ does not belong there: a name or directory that does not match, or a file such as a binary that a project does not hold.
findings.why: References and tools find records by ID, directory and file name.
suggestions: Rename or move the file as the evidence shows, or move a file that does not belong out of the project. Originals are not kept in the repository.

findings.message: A record points at a record that is missing or is of the wrong kind.
findings.why: The link between your evidence and its source is broken, so anything relying on it cannot be traced.
suggestions: Point the reference at the right record, or remove it.

findings.message: A record has a field the record format does not define. The field is kept as it is.
findings.why: A misspelled field name means the value you meant to record is not read.
suggestions: Check the spelling. Put a field of your own under `x` with a namespaced name such as `myname.note`.

findings.message: A heading in rules.md is not a rule heading.
findings.why: Reports and records cite standing rules by ID, so a rule without one cannot be cited.
suggestions: Write each rule heading as `## RULE-001 Title`.

findings.message: A rule ID in rules.md is used twice.
findings.why: A report or record citing this ID could mean either rule.
suggestions: Give the later rule a number that has never been used.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: Lists the passages, notes, claims and citations that rest on a source file or source since retired, on page text that has changed since a passage was captured, or on a passage captured before the source's details changed.
limits: A citation that names no passage is taken to rest on its source's files retired after the citation was recorded. Stemma cannot yet record that you have looked, so a finding stays listed. Damaged source files are reported by source.pages and source.held.

findings.message: This rests on a source file or source that has since been replaced or retired.
findings.why: What you read, quoted or relied on may differ in what replaced it, so it needs looking at again.
suggestions: Compare what you took from it with what replaced it, then correct or retire this item if it no longer holds. Stemma cannot yet record that you have looked, so the finding stays listed.

findings.message: The text of a page or section changed after a passage this rests on was captured from it.
findings.why: What you read, quoted or relied on may differ in what replaced it, so it needs looking at again.
suggestions: Look at the page, capture the passage again, and retire the old passage and anything copied from it that no longer holds.

findings.message: The source's details changed after a passage this rests on was captured.
findings.why: What you read, quoted or relied on may differ in what replaced it, so it needs looking at again.
suggestions: Check that the passage still belongs to the source as it is now recorded, and capture it again if it does.

findings.message: Whether what this rests on has changed could not be checked: something it depends on cannot be read.
findings.why: What you read, quoted or relied on may differ in what replaced it, so it needs looking at again.
suggestions: Repair the unreadable file first (see the record.valid and source.pages findings), then run `check` again.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: Where a source file marks footnotes, each marker has its note and each note its marker.
limits: It applies only to notes the conversion could determine. It says nothing about pages whose notes are marked as undetermined.

findings.message: A note marker in the text has no note on its page or section.
findings.why: A marker without its note, or a note without its marker, suggests text was lost or put in the wrong stream in conversion.
suggestions: Compare the page with the original. The note may continue from or onto another page, or the conversion may have lost it.

findings.message: A note has no marker in the text of its page or section.
findings.why: A marker without its note, or a note without its marker, suggests text was lost or put in the wrong stream in conversion.
suggestions: Compare the page with the original. If the note continues from an earlier page, mark its block continued.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: Each cited source must have source files in the project that hold text and are not damaged.
limits: It does not show that the text is a faithful reading of the original: Stemma never compares text with page images. It does not show that a source supports a sentence. It reads citation records only.

findings.message: A cited source has no source file in the project, so this citation is unchecked.
findings.why: Without the source's text in the project, nobody can compare this citation with the source, so it is unchecked.
suggestions: Capture the source: `ingest`, or `source convert <original> --source <id>`. For a book held only on paper, supply a transcription made by a recognition tool or typed. Writing can carry on meanwhile.

findings.message: A cited source's files hold no text, so this citation is unchecked.
findings.why: Without the source's text in the project, nobody can compare this citation with the source, so it is unchecked.
suggestions: Capture a copy of the source whose text can be read, or supply a transcription.

findings.message: Whether this cited source's text is here could not be checked: a source file's manifest cannot be read.
findings.why: Without the source's text in the project, nobody can compare this citation with the source, so it is unchecked.
suggestions: Repair the unreadable file first (see the record.valid finding), then run `check` again.

findings.message: A cited source has a source file that is damaged, so it is not used and this citation is unchecked.
findings.why: Without the source's text in the project, nobody can compare this citation with the source, so it is unchecked.
suggestions: See the source.pages and record.valid findings on that source file. Restore it from git, or record your own edit with `source seal`.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: Printed page labels in a source file must run on sensibly, and must agree with any page number marked on the page.
limits: Pages with no established label are left out. A finding may be a misprint or a missing leaf in the original: look at the page.

findings.message: Two pages in sequence carry the same printed label.
findings.why: Citations name printed pages. A wrong page label makes a wrong page reference pass, or a right one fail.
suggestions: Look at the page images. Correct the page map (`source label`), or leave a page without a label if its number is not established.

findings.message: Printed page labels go backwards.
findings.why: Citations name printed pages. A wrong page label makes a wrong page reference pass, or a right one fail.
suggestions: Look at the page images. A second numbering bound into one file can do this: label only the pages of the work you cite.

findings.message: Printed page numbers advance by more than the pages do, as when pages are missing from the original or a label is wrong.
findings.why: Citations name printed pages. A wrong page label makes a wrong page reference pass, or a right one fail.
suggestions: Nothing in the text shows that the pages run on. If leaves are missing from your copy, capture a complete one; if a label is wrong, correct the page map (`source label`).

findings.message: A page number printed on a page differs from the label recorded for that page.
findings.why: Citations name printed pages. A wrong page label makes a wrong page reference pass, or a right one fail.
suggestions: Look at the page image and correct whichever is wrong.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: Each source file must be tied to an original that its source's upstream records name, and a recorded fresh conversion of that original must still apply and agree.
limits: It reads the recorded comparison: it does not open the original. A conversion that agrees repeats any mistake already in the original's text layer.

findings.message: A source file was converted from an original that none of the source's upstream records names.
findings.why: The chain from the original to your citation rests on the source file being what the original gives.
suggestions: Check which original is right. Record its upstream (`ingest --plan`), or retire this source file.

findings.message: A fresh conversion of the original does not give the committed text, after a person's corrections are undone.
findings.why: The chain from the original to your citation rests on the source file being what the original gives.
suggestions: Look at the differing readings. If a person edited the words, mark the change as a correction; otherwise restore the file, or convert the original again and retire this one.

findings.message: The text or the tools changed after the last fresh conversion was compared, so it no longer says anything.
findings.why: The chain from the original to your citation rests on the source file being what the original gives.
suggestions: Run `source verify <text id> --original <file>`, or `ingest` with the originals.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.

summary: Each source file's manifest and its page or section files must agree: none missing, extra, out of order, unreadable or edited without being sealed, and as many pages as the original has.
limits: It shows that the files are complete and unchanged, not that their text is right. The count of pages in the original is the one recorded at conversion.

findings.message: A page or section file that the manifest lists is missing.
findings.why: Every quotation and page check reads these files. A missing, reordered or changed part can hide or invent what the source says, so this source file is not used until it is sound.
suggestions: Restore the file from git.

findings.message: A page or section file differs from the digest its manifest records.
findings.why: Every quotation and page check reads these files. A missing, reordered or changed part can hide or invent what the source says, so this source file is not used until it is sound.
suggestions: If you meant to edit it, record the edit with `source seal <text id> --actor person:<name>`. Otherwise restore it from git.

findings.message: A page or section file is in the source directory but not in its manifest.
findings.why: Every quotation and page check reads these files. A missing, reordered or changed part can hide or invent what the source says, so this source file is not used until it is sound.
suggestions: Remove the file, or convert the source again.

findings.message: A page or section file cannot be read.
findings.why: Every quotation and page check reads these files. A missing, reordered or changed part can hide or invent what the source says, so this source file is not used until it is sound.
suggestions: Restore the file from git.

findings.message: A page or section file's place does not agree with its name or its manifest.
findings.why: Every quotation and page check reads these files. A missing, reordered or changed part can hide or invent what the source says, so this source file is not used until it is sound.
suggestions: Restore the files from git; their order is part of what is checked.

findings.message: The manifest does not list the pages or sections in sequence.
findings.why: Every quotation and page check reads these files. A missing, reordered or changed part can hide or invent what the source says, so this source file is not used until it is sound.
suggestions: Restore the manifest from git.

findings.message: The pages of the source file do not match the number of pages in the original.
findings.why: Every quotation and page check reads these files. A missing, reordered or changed part can hide or invent what the source says, so this source file is not used until it is sound.
suggestions: Restore the missing pages from git, or convert the original again. A source file that holds only some pages must say so.

findings.message: A source file's manifest or a part breaks the source file format, so its completeness could not be checked.
findings.why: Every quotation and page check reads these files. A missing, reordered or changed part can hide or invent what the source says, so this source file is not used until it is sound.
suggestions: See the record.valid finding and correct it.

findings.message: The check itself failed while running, so this was not checked.
findings.why: This is a defect in Stemma, not a pass.
suggestions: Report the defect together with the Stemma version.
